recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce expand.limitedExpansion wording for FHIR-14703 unless the work group reopens the later FHIR-16449 count-based replacement decision.
issue_request: FHIR-14703 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 vocab change request for ValueSet $expand. It asked to clarify that a server chooses the size and membership of a limited expansion, and to adjust expand.limitedExpansion documentation to say that the operation parameter overrides ExpansionProfile.limitedExpansion if present.
initial_application: The Jira comment says the change was pre-applied in svn 13351. Git commit d90f55e1cbc897c77c5188342e1d43353f38f2c3 matches that history and added the requested server-discretion and ExpansionProfile.limitedExpansion override wording to source/valueset/valueset-spreadsheet.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-16449 later reached Published/Persuasive with Modification for the same ValueSet $expand parameter family, directing removal of ValueSet.$expand.limitedExpansion because the server decides when an expansion is too expensive and clients already have count for partial results. Commit af02669d4245739a4c4ea146117faca6ad0fb4c9 removed the parameter and added count-based limited-subset wording. FHIR-16449 is already represented on the combined branch by commit 3731ea54fec8bf1099c9605ea448e0d33c80963f.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active current source has no limitedExpansion parameter, and source/valueset/operationdefinition-ValueSet-expand.xml says oversized expansions are at server discretion while clients may use offset/count or count for limited-purpose subsets.

related_jiras.note: Removed ValueSet.$expand.limitedExpansion and shifted limited-subset guidance to count; already audited on the combined branch, so it was not republished here.
